entities.name: Syrus of Genoa
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Saint Syrus of Genoa was a priest and later bishop of Genoa during the fourth century AD.

Syrus was born in the late 4th century AD, but the exact date is unknown. He became the bishop of Genoa around 380-390 AD and played a significant role in the city's religious life.

During his tenure, Syrus oversaw the construction of several churches and monasteries, including the Church of San Lorenzo, which still stands today. He also worked to promote the spread of Christianity throughout the region.

Syrus' legacy as a bishop and his contributions to the development of Christianity in Genoa have endured for centuries. He is remembered as a devoted servant of God and a champion of faith.

"We must not forget that our Lord Jesus Christ has died for us, and we must always be grateful for His sacrifice." - Saint Syrus of Genoa
